newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boeing CEO expects EU to look favourably on merger.
newsitem.headline: Boeing CEO expects EU to look favourably on merger.

text.p: Boeing chief executive Phil Condit said on Wednesday that he was confident European Union competition regulators would eventually approve Boeing's merger with McDonnell-Douglas.

Condit, who met EU competition commissioner Karel van Miert on Tuesday, said the meeting was "good", and that he expected Brussels to reach a favourable conclusion after a months-long review of the merger.

"It was one of those meetings where I stated where I was coming from, and he described to me the process that they would go through -- and that of course is a complete review," Condit told a news conference during an economic conference here.
"That is of course exactly what we expected," he added.
Asked whether he expected the review to come out in favour of the merger Condit said: "That's exactly right."
Van Miert is expected to announce next week that the commission would extend its initial one-month investigation into the $50 billion merger of Boeing and McDonnell-Douglas.
He was quoted by Wednesday's Financial Times saying that problems "still remain".
